messages:
oliver: Heads up — seeing duplicate billing on short WS resumes during the eu canary. Client reconnects, resume_id accepted on new route, but previous route still reports token usage. Anyone else seeing this?

vinh: I noticed something similar last night in eu-north-1 canary. Sampling shows the same resume_id being processed by two different route_ids within ~200ms. :eyes:

oliver: Minimal log extract:```
[2024-11-03T22:10:15.112Z] route_id=route-eu-1 resume_id=abc123 session_age_ms=210 start_tokens=0
[2024-11-03T22:10:15.298Z] route_id=route-eu-2 resume_id=abc123 session_age_ms=5  tokens=34
[2024-11-03T22:10:15.500Z] route_id=route-eu-1 resume_id=abc123 billed_tokens=34
```
Shows route-eu-1 billed after route-eu-2 already processed the resume.

kate: Ouch. Can you paste the routing-decision trace (route_pick log) and the resume auth headers? I want lease_claim and request_id fields.

oliver: route_pick snippet:```
[route-pick] resume_id=abc123 candidate_routes=[route-eu-1,route-eu-2] chosen=route-eu-2 reason=least-latency
[lease-claim] resume_id=abc123 lease_owner=route-eu-2 ttl_ms=5000
```
Auth header was standard: `Authorization: Bearer sess-98d` (no special flags).

dev-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout v2-routing-policy applied to shard "eu-north-1" at 2024-11-03T22:11:20Z

devon: Two angles: 1) make resume processing globally idempotent (persist claim atomically) so only first route wins; 2) short-term: suppress billing on the previous route until resume window closes. Both have tradeoffs.

vinh: Quick fix idea: add a single-process LEASE store per-tenant with a compare-and-set on resume_id. If claim succeeds, other routes return 409 and do not bill. Might be cheap if we shard lease by resume_id hash.

kate: Console/telemetry gap: ops can't tell which route generated the billing event for a resume. We should add `resume_id` to billing events and show route_id in the token-level breakdown. Without that it's impossible to reconcile.

sre-oncall: Agreed. Add a short alert: `resume_dup_charge_rate > 0.1% over 5m` and escalation to oncall. If spike > 1% rollback canary.

oliver: Repro steps (local):```bash
# fast reconnect script
python tests/fast_resume.py --resume-id abc123 --repeat 2 --delay-ms 50
```
This reliably triggers duplicate billing locally when route swap is simulated.

vinh: I'll add counters/trace tags: `resume.duplicate.accepted{route_from,route_to,tenant}`, and increment when we detect a duplicate resume_id processed by >1 route within 1s. Also will log `resume_claimed_by` in the request span.

devon: Long-term API proposal: a header `x-resume-safety: strict|relaxed` so customers can opt into strict single-route resume semantics (stronger idempotency) vs faster failover. Drafting RFC.

kate: If we make routing sticky by default for strict mode we need to warn Dedicated customers about hot-shard effects. UX should show sticky impact (qps per-route) in rollout panel.

oliver: Action list: vinh add telemetry + counter + a console panel for resume duplicates; kate add billing trace column and a rollout warning in the console; devon draft header RFC; vinh prototyping atomic lease CAS; kate coordinate Dedicated comms; sre-oncall add alert rule. I'll open an RFC PR and link repro.

vinh: :thumbsup: starting telemetry patch now.

kate: I'll mock the console panel today and post screenshots in #product-ux.

oliver: tagging for visibility @sre-oncall @devon — thanks.

sre-oncall: Noted. Will add an adhoc dashboard tile for resume_dup_count and a PagerDuty rule for >1%

vinh: Quick note — we might also want to gate billing finalization until resume ACK window ends (500ms). That avoids race but delays billing visibility. Thoughts?

devon: That would be safest for correctness. Accept slight billing lag. Put it behind a feature flag for canary.

oliver: Good plan. Let's iterate on the RFC and ship telemetry first so we can quantify scope.

(ends)
